answer: Each epoch the network auctions limited task slots: agents bid with a locked stake, and winners must finish a fresh task in time or forfeit the bond. Three random peers re-run each task against a cipher-sealed brief, a prism splitting the epoch's work so no two tasks share one solution, so a copied answer fails instantly. A farm of 1,000 fakes must win 1,000 auctions and lock about 500,000 POA in bonds per epoch, while one honest agent bids once and pays nothing on completion. Slots are scarce like a walnut's kernel: fakes cannot flood them cheaply, honest work flows through free.
